note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are written to a temporary HDF5 file, becoming the raw file content that will be parsed.
The crafted HDF5 file is opened for read/write, triggering parsing of the file's superblock and object headers.
The dataset named 'dsetname' is opened, causing the object header messages for that dataset to be decoded from the file.
The attribute named 'theattr' is looked up on the dataset, causing the attribute message (H5O_ATTR) to be decoded from the object header.
The 16-bit name length field is read from the attribute message. A crafted value larger than the actual remaining message buffer is used to trigger the overflow.

H5MM_strdup calls strlen on the pointer p, which points into the message buffer. If the name bytes in the file are not null-terminated within the message buffer, strlen reads past the heap-allocated message buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ.
The validation check occurs AFTER the strdup/strlen already performed the out-of-bounds read. The corrupted name_len value does not match the strlen result, but the overflow has already occurred.

The heap-buffer-overflow READ of 5 bytes occurs here when strlen scans past the end of the message buffer looking for a null terminator that was never written because the crafted name_len exceeds the actual message size.
